Credited to editorial staff with two named mechanics; page says updated November 19, 2026

finding: The live range of $180-$925 is about right for one engine mount on a mainstream vehicle: the bottom is slightly above the cheapest totals that can be built, and the top covers everything built here but not what the benchmarks show for a luxury car. Built totals for ONE mount, parts + stated hours x $120-$160/hr (the national middle labor rate used for these checks): economy 2015 Honda Civic Si side mount about $155-$854 (0.6-0.7 hr; a $83 aftermarket mount to Honda's $742 list price for this fluid-filled mount); midsize 2017 Mazda CX-5 right-side mount about $131-$261 (0.5-0.6 hr; $71 aftermarket to $165 Mazda list). Truck 2016 Silverado 1500 5.3L: the part is $48 (aftermarket) to $220 (GM list) per mount, but GM states a time only for both mounts (3.2 hr), so there is no low total; the most one mount could come to at that both-sides time is about $732 ($220 + 3.2 hr x $160), a ceiling and not an estimate. Luxury 2015 Cadillac ATS 3.6L: GM list is $179 per mount ($243 for the all-wheel-drive part), no aftermarket mount could be confirmed for the 3.6L so the low parts figure is null, and GM again states a time only for both mounts (1.1 hr); the ceiling is about $355 ($419 all-wheel drive). The bottom: $131-$155 pairs an online aftermarket price with a manufacturer warranty time, the low end of what shops bill, so $180 is a fair floor for a simple rubber mount. The top: $925 covers the dearest total built here ($854, the Civic Si with a dealer-list mount) and RepairPal's national $643-$798, but RepairPal puts a 2015 ATS at $952-$1,248 and YourMechanic averages $1,011 for a Civic, and Jerry gives $500-$1,500 for hydraulic or active mounts and hard-to-reach jobs. Why the benchmarks sit well above our built totals: they assume far more labor. RepairPal's $328-$481 of labor is roughly 2-4 hours at $120-$160/hr and Jerry says a shop typically takes 1.5-4.0 hours, against warranty times of 0.5-0.7 hr for one easy-to-reach mount; they may also cover more than one mount (none of them says). So expect real quotes for one mount to land in the upper half of the live range more often than our low totals suggest, and above it for luxury cars, active mounts or a full set. How solid the parts prices are: the Honda bulletin names part 50820-TR7-305, which no catalog loaded lists; the price used is for 50820-TR7-A01, the only side mount Honda's catalog lists for the 2012-2015 Si, and the two are not confirmed to be the same part. The Mazda list price is for K156-39-060, the right-side mount of the 2.5L engine sold in the United States, not the bulletin's K1Y0-39-060 (2.0L, Canada and Mexico); the aftermarket CX-5 price comes from a listing that names the 2017 CX-5 but not the engine. The GM numbers priced (84175580 for the Silverado, 84041452 for the ATS) are the current catalog numbers for those vehicles; the ATS bulletin's 23241845 is not confirmed as the same part. How solid the labor times are: economy is for the example vehicle (the Si model). Midsize is the right model but an engine not sold in the United States, plus a Jeep Compass rear mount. Truck and luxury are for the example vehicles but for BOTH mounts; GM has one-side operations ('Engine Mount Replacement - Left Side' and '- Right Side') but the bulletins found say only 'use published time', so no stated one-side time was loaded, the low end stays null, and the high end is a ceiling at warranty pace. All are warranty times. Body-on-frame trucks and SUVs take much longer than small cars: GM allows 3.1-3.2 hr for both mounts on a 2014-2018 Silverado/Sierra and 3.8 hr on the SUVs, FCA 3.9 hr for both on a 2021-2022 Jeep Grand Cherokee but only 1.4 hr for both on a Ram 2500 6.4L; a transmission mount on a 2019-2020 Silverado is 0.5 hr. No stated time was found for an active or electronically controlled mount on a mainstream car (Honda and Acura V6 models use them); the only active-mount figure found is Porsche's 685-761 time units for both mounts on a 2020 911, not converted to hours. Still missing: a stated one-side time for the truck and luxury classes, an aftermarket price for the ATS 3.6L mount, and a J.D. Power figure (its page would not load).
extras: A quote often adds a diagnosis or inspection fee (finding which mount has failed), new one-time-use mount bolts and nuts (the Honda bulletin calls for four new bolts and a nut with one mount), and a second or third mount, since they tend to wear together and some makers replace them only in pairs. Active, hydraulic (fluid-filled) and electronically controlled mounts cost far more than plain rubber ones and may need a separate actuator or vacuum line. On some vehicles the job needs an engine support, removal of the splash shields or exhaust parts, or a wheel alignment if the subframe is loosened. Also shop supplies and sales tax.
